messages:
Maya (design): tl;dr: on very narrow phones the Resources table breaks layout. Instead of a bottomsheet, proposing a stacked card pattern that surfaces each row as a full-width card you swipe vertically. Keeps toolbar intact and reduces modal complexity.
Omar (frontend): interesting. Cards avoid overlays but could be heavier DOM. How do we surface bulk actions and multi-select?
Maya (design): multi-select via long-press to enter selection mode (toolbar morphs to selection bar). Primary action stays sticky at bottom of viewport.
Sam (product): curious about discoverability for filters and sorts. Power users need quick access.
Maya (design): add a small floating filter FAB in the top-right of the toolbar that opens an inline sheet anchored to toolbar (not full-screen). That keeps filters visible and discoverable.
Ben (pm): keyboard/viewport on iOS still a worry. If toolbar morphs and we show inline sheet, keyboard can cover inputs.
Omar (frontend): solution: anchor inputs above keyboard using visualViewport API; fall back to 100vh calculations for older browsers. Also test WKWebView on iOS.
ux-bot: metric note: 18% of visits to this page are <=380px (30d).
Maya (design): accessibility: each card must be a single accessible listitem with proper heading, actions have 44px targets. When entering selection mode, announce state and focus on the first selected item.
Omar (frontend): agree. We'll implement roving tabindex for card actions and use aria-pressed for selected state.
Sam (product): copy: "Resources" ambiguous. Propose "Workloads" or simply "Jobs" depending on context.
Maya (design): prefer "Workloads" for consistency.
Ben (pm): truncation: long IDs should show compact, with an inline reveal affordance labeled "show full id" for clarity (not just an icon).
Maya (design): yes—truncate at 20 chars, reveal inline; screen readers see full id in offscreen text.
Omar (frontend): plan: prototype card stack + toolbar FAB by Tue, run quick accessibility pass Wed, test on Pixel 4a and iPhone SE. If good, A/B on mobile canary.
Maya (design): thanks — will post mocks and interaction video in #design later today. @Omar please attach prototype link when ready. :raised_hands:
